title: Measuring the Marginal Detection Benefit of Sandboxed Emulation for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the marginal detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator when analyzing identical LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded outcomes lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative results, provider-call accounting, an explanation of provider-call audit fields, and an evidence-grounded interpretation that identifies the validator ceiling and the curated task bank as the primary reasons for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime. Reproducibility artifacts and the execution manifest are archived alongside the preregistration.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and NetOps workflows. Safety and operational trustworthiness require that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow-order constraints, invariants (for example, keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties. A common operational architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports argue for this workflow-centred approach and note that the marginal value of emulation depends on validator coverage, emulator fidelity, and input distribution [1]–[3].

We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to answer a focused question under shared_initial_candidate semantics: when the identical generated candidate is evaluated by (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) aggregated across tasks? Our contributions are (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete run accounting; (3) a concise explanation—supported by archived traces—of why the guarded-stage marginal effect was negligible in this experimental regime; and (4) reproducibility pointers for targeted follow-up experiments.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps documents both architectural proposals and prototype systems that pair generation with validators, emulators, or repair loops to raise assurance [1]. Research in verifier-assisted LLM workflows (generate→validate→repair) and NetOps validation tools highlights a recurring trade-off: static rule-based validators can cover many syntactic and workflow patterns, while emulation can reveal temporal or stateful behaviors that static rules struggle to express [2]. Empirical prototype studies and surveys further show heterogeneous gains from emulation: some task regimes show large guarded benefits; others show most errors already captured by static analysis, so emulation yields limited marginal value [3]. Our paired shared_initial_candidate design isolates only downstream guarded-stage contributions—thereby complementing prior, often unpaired, evaluations.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest used for power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points). Inclusion/exclusion, missingness, contamination controls, multiplicity handling, and the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) were fixed before execution.

Task bank, vendor abstraction, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Confirmatory tasks (Npairs = 720) were deterministically generated from intent_configuration_repair_v1 and cover three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task includes initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). The preregistration enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair the system performed exactly one model call to produce a sampled candidate, and that identical candidate was provided to both analysis conditions (validator-only and guarded). This isolates downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or repair-stage invocation) as the only permissible source of between-condition discordance.

Model and orchestration. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Model configuration archived the requested max_output_tokens = 2000 and left temperature unspecified (recorded as null), which indicates no explicit temperature was set by the client; it does not imply provider-side determinism. The orchestration adapter family recorded for the run is hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Provider-call auditing and stage accounting were recorded in the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts.

Baseline validator and guarded emulation harness. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic rule-based engine performing: vendor-CLI syntactic parsing; per-command canonicalization; sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence; workflow atomicity constraints; group-level activity invariants; protected-interface enforcement; and final-state conformance tests. The validator returns a binary detected/not-detected flag and emits a detailed validator_trace for each evaluated candidate.

The guarded pipeline executes the baseline validator and then runs an automated sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology template and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulator produces runtime observations (interface admin transitions, transient concurrent states, MTU/VLAN application effects, observable connectivity implications). The emulation harness maps runtime observations to runtime-observation rules; when such rules expose policy or safety violations not encoded in the static validator, the guarded pipeline records a guarded detection. The emulation mapping is intentionally conservative for this study.

Repair policy and provider-call accounting. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task, only after guarded-condition observations are available. Provider-call auditing in deterministic_reconciliation reports model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1; thus a single repair-stage call occurred across the confirmatory set. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, any discordant guarded-only detection must be attributable to a guarded emulation observation or to that unique repair invocation; both are traceable in the archived episode artifacts.

Provider-call audit clarification. The execution artifacts include an aggregated provider_call_audit object whose keys may appear ambiguous without context. In our run: "shared_initial_generation" = 720 denotes the number of distinct initial-generation model calls that produced shared candidates (one per pair). The audit field labeled condition_counts includes two entries: "shared":720 and "guarded":1. Here "shared" refers to the shared_initial_generation stage (the one call per pair whose output was reused across both analysis conditions). The audit entry labeled "guarded":1 refers to a repair-stage call that is attributable to the guarded workflow (repair-stage model invocation). In short, the audit distinguishes (a) the per-pair shared initial generation volume and (b) additional repair-stage calls invoked only under the guarded condition; the archived deterministic_reconciliation.json contains the authoritative mapping.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). Analysis artifacts report n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are reproduced verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Deterministic reconciliation reports completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Because generation variability was removed by design, the single n10 discordant pair is linked to the unique repair-stage invocation or to an emulation observation not codified as a validator violation. The execution bundle contains the raw per-episode record for that discordant pair; an auditor can locate the unique raw_results.jsonl entry with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1 and inspect its validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields to determine whether the guarded detection arose from a repair-altered candidate or a guarded emulation observation. The archived deterministic_reconciliation.json (and analysis artifacts) provide the authoritative provider-call mapping.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded explanation for the negligible guarded marginal effect. The archived artifacts point to three complementary factors:

1) Validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator explicitly encoded the workflow constraints exercised by the curated tasks (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). Representative validator_trace objects (parsing counts and violation_count = 0 in the majority of episodes) show that most shared_initial candidates already satisfied the validator’s rule set, producing a baseline success rate of 719/720 (0.9986111111111111) and leaving minimal headroom for guarded-stage detections.

2) Curated, parser-validated confirmatory bank. Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after deterministic reseeding; the confirmatory sample thus excluded parser-invalid or highly noisy intents. This constrained design reduces the prevalence of runtime-only failures that emulation would detect in broader or adversarial distributions.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. By reusing the same sampled candidate across both conditions we intentionally isolated downstream guarded-stage signals. Provider-call auditing confirms only one repair-stage call occurred (repair = 1), which aligns with the single n10 discordant count; archived traces permit locating and inspecting that single episode to determine proximate cause.

Operational implications. In operational regimes where a high-coverage static validator is maintained and inputs are prevalidated, an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may provide little incremental detection benefit at scale. This conclusion is conditional: in noisy natural-language input pipelines, adversarial or fuzzed cases, broader multi-vendor diversity, or workflows with long-lived state transitions, guarded emulation is more likely to surface violations absent from static rule-sets. Practically, operators should (a) invest in validator coverage tailored to expected intents for low-latency/high-throughput pipelines, (b) reserve guarded emulation for high-risk or high-impact changes, and (c) use adversarial test banks to locate validator gaps. The archived representative traces supply concrete seed cases for such adversarial generation.

Limitations tied to the archived evidence. The finding of a near-zero marginal guarded effect is specific to the preregistered task bank, validator implementation, declared/requested model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the empirical estimate (~0.0014) is far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero result for this experimental regime rather than evidence that guarded stages are unnecessary in general. Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching are residual uncertainties despite reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that compared a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); deterministic reconciliation links the single guarded-only detection to that unique repair-stage invocation or to a guarded emulation observation, and the per-episode artifacts permit independent inspection. We interpret these results as arising from validator ceiling effects and the curated task design. Follow-up work should target adversarial and production-like task banks, multi-validator ensembles, and higher-fidelity emulation modalities; the archived execution bundle provides seed traces and the canonical inputs needed to pursue these extensions.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This paper reports an autonomous post-lock experiment run under the frozen initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration was fixed prior to confirmatory execution). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. The execution manifest and archived artifact bundle (referenced in the paper) contain the full per-file provenance and run accounting.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate guarded-stage contributions but remove between-condition generation variability; this design decision constrains the source of discordance to downstream guarded observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived control-plane subtleties is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could yield different outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.
Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation; these are documented in the execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
